/-!
# Erdős Problem 982

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/982](https://www.erdosproblems.com/982)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos982

/--
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then some vertex has at least
$\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ different distances to other vertices.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_982 (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (p : Fin n → ℝ²) (hp : Function.Injective p)
    (hp' : EuclideanGeometry.IsConvexPolygon p) :
    ∃ (i : Fin n), { d : ℝ | ∃ j : Fin n, j ≠ i ∧ d = dist (p i) (p j) }.ncard ≥ n / 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos982

reformulations.difference: The Lean hypothesis requires the supplied enumeration p to list a convex polygon in cyclic order, up to reversal. The source describes a point set forming a convex polygon, without prescribing its labeling.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every convex polygon admits a cyclic labeling. Relabeling by a permutation e sends the distance set at i for p ∘ e to the distance set at e i for p, preserving its cardinality and the existential conclusion. In scratch.lean, I proved this set equality and the ↔ between the universally quantified statement using IsConvexPolygon p and the version using ∃ e : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), IsConvexPolygon (p ∘ e). Thus the ordered-list formulation loses no configurations.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the source's conjecture, which remains marked open. The strict orientation condition matches the cited paper's convention: convex position excludes collinear triples. The distance set is finite, so Set.ncard's infinite-set default cannot occur; injectivity and j ≠ i exclude zero distances. Successful Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and boundaries.lean verify these facts, natural division versus floor, the Euclidean metric, the n = 3 conclusion, and a concrete triangle satisfying both hypotheses. The paper also includes n = 2; that omitted case is automatically true and was proved separately, so the n ≥ 3 restriction does not change the conjecture. The source's disproved stronger variants are not asserted by this file.
